title: A 16-Year-Old Guitar Shredder From Thailand Just Won America's Got Talent
summary:
Imagine standing backstage at America's Got Talent. Your hands are sweaty. Your guitar is heavy on your hip. Then you walk out, and 21 million people will watch what happens next.

That's what happened to Nene Royal. She's 16 years old and from Thailand. When she first walked onstage, she looked shy. Then she picked up her electric guitar and started playing "Zombie" by the Cranberries. It was loud, fast, and face-melting. The whole audience stood up and cheered.

Nene kept rocking all season. She played songs by Soundgarden, Muse, and the White Stripes. In the finale, she sang with Linkin Park. Then host Terry Crews said her name — she won! She got one million dollars and became the first Thai winner ever on the show.

"When Terry Crews announced my name, I'm shocked. I just faint," she said, laughing. Her school friends keep texting her, but she's too busy to read it all.

Nene started playing guitar when she was 7. Now she wants to make a rock album and go on tour. First? Maybe Disneyland. Or sleep!
why_it_matters: It shows that a skill you start practising as a kid — like an instrument — can grow into something huge, so the hobbies you begin in school really can change your future.

background_read: America's Got Talent (a TV talent show in the United States where singers, dancers and musicians perform for a big audience) has been on TV for many years, and about 21 million people watch the final.
Terry Crews (an American actor and comedian who hosts the show) is the person who reads out the winner's name.
Nene played 'Zombie', a famous 1990s song by the Cranberries (an Irish rock band), and in the finale she shared the stage with Linkin Park, a huge American rock band.
Article_Structure: WHO: Nene Royal, a 16-year-old electric guitarist from Thailand
WHAT: She won the TV contest America's Got Talent and took home one million dollars
WHERE: On the America's Got Talent stage, watched by around 21 million people
WHY: Her loud, fast, face-melting playing made the audience stand and cheer, and she became the first Thai winner ever on the show

perspectives.description: They think it is amazing that a shy 16-year-old can win a giant TV contest just by playing guitar really well.

perspectives.perspective: People who worry about young stars
perspectives.description: They point out that being famous at 16 brings a lot of pressure, with millions watching and messages coming in all the time.
They notice that the show has made young performers into stars before, and that winning is often less about age and more about years of practice.
